CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFFILE

CFFILE does all the file work a template needs. The ACTION attribute picks the operation: UPLOAD saves a file sent from a browser form, READ and READBINARY load a file into a variable, WRITE and APPEND create or extend a text file, and COPY, MOVE, RENAME and DELETE do what their names say.

Category

File, directory and system

Syntax

<CFFILE ACTION="UPLOAD"
    FILEFIELD="formfield"
    DESTINATION="full_path_name"
    NAMECONFLICT="behavior"
    ACCEPT="mime_type/file_type"
    MODE="permission"
    ATTRIBUTES="file_attributes">

<CFFILE ACTION="READ" FILE="full_path_name" VARIABLE="var_name">
<CFFILE ACTION="READBINARY" FILE="full_path_name" VARIABLE="var_name">
<CFFILE ACTION="WRITE" FILE="full_path_name" OUTPUT="content"
    ADDNEWLINE="Yes/No" MODE="permission" ATTRIBUTES="file_attributes">
<CFFILE ACTION="APPEND" FILE="full_path_name" OUTPUT="content"
    ADDNEWLINE="Yes/No" MODE="permission" ATTRIBUTES="file_attributes">
<CFFILE ACTION="COPY" SOURCE="full_path_name" DESTINATION="full_path_name">
<CFFILE ACTION="MOVE" SOURCE="full_path_name" DESTINATION="full_path_name">
<CFFILE ACTION="RENAME" SOURCE="full_path_name" DESTINATION="full_path_name">
<CFFILE ACTION="DELETE" FILE="full_path_name">

Attributes

ACTION
Required. UPLOAD, READ, READBINARY, WRITE, APPEND, COPY, MOVE, RENAME or DELETE.
FILEFIELD
Required for UPLOAD. Name of the form field (INPUT TYPE="File") that holds the file. Give the name without pound signs.
DESTINATION
Required for UPLOAD, COPY, MOVE, RENAME. Target directory or full file name. If it is a directory, the original file name is kept.
NAMECONFLICT
Optional, default "Error". For UPLOAD, what to do when the file already exists: Error (throw an exception), Skip (save nothing), Overwrite, or MakeUnique (add a number to the name, as in photo1.gif).
ACCEPT
Optional. For UPLOAD, comma-separated MIME types to accept, such as "image/gif, image/jpeg" or "image/*". Anything else is refused with an exception.
FILE
Required for READ, READBINARY, WRITE, APPEND, DELETE. Full path of the file.
VARIABLE
Required for READ, READBINARY. Variable that receives the contents: a string for READ, a binary object for READBINARY (see ToBase64 and IsBinary).
OUTPUT
Required for WRITE, APPEND. The text to write. A binary object is written byte for byte.
ADDNEWLINE
Optional, default "Yes". For WRITE and APPEND, Yes adds a newline after OUTPUT.
SOURCE
Required for COPY, MOVE, RENAME. Full path of the existing file.
MODE
Optional. UNIX permissions as three octal digits, such as 644 or 755.
ATTRIBUTES
Optional. Windows file attributes (ReadOnly, Hidden, Normal). Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.

Usage

Always use full paths; GetTempDirectory, ExpandPath and GetDirectoryFromPath(GetCurrentTemplatePath()) help you build them. Failures throw an Application exception with the message "Error processing CFFILE" and the reason in the detail.

After an UPLOAD, the variables below describe what happened. They are in the CFFILE structure, and also in File for templates written for ColdFusion 3.x:

Variable Contents
CFFILE.ClientDirectory, ClientFile, ClientFileName, ClientFileExt Where the file came from on the browser's machine
CFFILE.ServerDirectory, ServerFile, ServerFileName, ServerFileExt Where it was saved on the server
CFFILE.AttemptedServerFile The name it would have had without MakeUnique
CFFILE.ContentType, ContentSubType MIME type, such as image and gif
CFFILE.FileSize, OldFileSize Size of the upload, and of the file it replaced
CFFILE.FileExisted, FileWasSaved, FileWasOverwritten, FileWasRenamed, FileWasAppended YES or NO
CFFILE.TimeCreated, TimeLastModified, DateLastAccessed Date/time values

The upload form must use METHOD="POST" and ENCTYPE="multipart/form-data". Restricting the tag is possible on the Basic Security page of the Administrator.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Scratch = GetTempDirectory() & "cffile_demo.txt">
<CFFILE ACTION="WRITE" FILE="#Scratch#" OUTPUT="Line 1: written #DateFormat(Now(), 'mmm d, yyyy')#">
<CFFILE ACTION="APPEND" FILE="#Scratch#" OUTPUT="Line 2: appended">
<CFFILE ACTION="READ" FILE="#Scratch#" VARIABLE="Contents">
<CFFILE ACTION="DELETE" FILE="#Scratch#">
<CFOUTPUT><P>WRITE, APPEND, READ and DELETE:</P><PRE>#HTMLEditFormat(Contents)#</PRE></CFOUTPUT>

<CFIF IsDefined("Form.Upload") AND Len(Form.Upload)>
  <CFFILE ACTION="UPLOAD" FILEFIELD="Upload" DESTINATION="#GetTempDirectory()#" NAMECONFLICT="MakeUnique">
  <CFOUTPUT>
  <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
  <TR><TD>ClientFile</TD><TD>#HTMLEditFormat(CFFILE.ClientFile)#</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>ServerFile</TD><TD>#HTMLEditFormat(CFFILE.ServerFile)#</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>FileSize</TD><TD>#CFFILE.FileSize# bytes</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>ContentType</TD><TD>#CFFILE.ContentType#/#CFFILE.ContentSubType#</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>FileWasRenamed</TD><TD>#CFFILE.FileWasRenamed#</TD></TR>
  </TABLE>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  <!--- This is only a demo: throw the upload away again --->
  <CFFILE ACTION="DELETE" FILE="#CFFILE.ServerDirectory#/#CFFILE.ServerFile#">
</CFIF>

<FORM ACTION="cffile.cfm" METHOD="POST" ENCTYPE="multipart/form-data">
Upload a small file: <INPUT TYPE="File" NAME="Upload">
<INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Upload">
</FORM>
